findings.title: Increment the retry counter atomically
findings.body: Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched before processing the batch. If two cron invocations overlap and both fail to schedule the same reminder, they can both read 0 and write 1, losing one failure. The reminder then survives despite having failed twice and receives additional scheduling attempts. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths rather than assigning a value from the stale snapshot.

findings.title: Keep retry bookkeeping failures from aborting the entire batch
findings.body: The catch block now awaits a database update without handling errors from that update. If the reminder has been deleted while scheduling was in progress (for example, by an overlapping cron's expired-reminder cleanup), Prisma's update throws because the row no longer exists. A database outage can likewise make both the original update and this recovery update fail. That exception escapes the per-reminder catch, aborting the handler and leaving every remaining reminder in the batch unprocessed; previously the catch logged the error and continued. Handle failures of the retry-count update separately so one reminder's bookkeeping failure does not stop the batch.
